title: Reasoning with Language Model Prompting: A Survey
best_for_zh: 想系统了解提示式推理方法、任务与比较方式的读者。
one_line: An ACL 2023 survey of prompting methods used to elicit and study reasoning in language models.
系统梳理如何用提示激发语言模型推理，并提供方法比较与学习资源。
why: It helps readers compare reasoning methods by what the prompt changes, which task is measured, and what evidence supports the claim.
inclusion_reason: An accepted ACL survey that gives readers a compact entry point to prompting-based reasoning methods, comparisons, and resources.

title: Problem
问题
html: Complex problems often require more than a direct answer, yet prompting studies use different tasks, prompt formats, model families, and evaluation choices. Those differences make it difficult to tell whether two papers are making the same claim when both say that a prompt improves reasoning. This ACL 2023 survey collects cutting-edge work on reasoning with language-model prompting so a reader can see what was compared, what task each comparison serves, and why the question was studied. The practical problem is not merely finding a named prompting method; it is judging the evidence attached to that method. The paper is a survey and resource overview, not a new model, a new prompting algorithm, or a dataset release.

复杂问题往往不只是直接给出答案；但不同提示研究采用的任务、提示格式、模型类型和评测选择并不相同。即使两篇论文都说某种提示改善了推理，这些差异也会让人难以判断它们是否在提出同一种结论。本文是 ACL 2023 的综述，汇集语言模型提示推理的前沿工作，使读者看清比较了什么、每个比较服务于什么任务，以及为何研究这一问题。真正需要解决的不只是找到一种有名称的提示方法，而是判断支撑该方法的证据。本文是综述和资源概览，不发布新模型、新提示算法或数据集。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html: The paper treats prompting as a way to study and elicit reasoning in language models rather than as a single interchangeable trick. Its contribution is a comparative synthesis of research works, paired with systematic resources for beginners and a discussion of why reasoning abilities may emerge. The central reading lens is to connect a prompting claim with the task, the model response, and the comparison that support it. That lens is useful because a prompt can change how a question is presented without making every task equally informative about reasoning. Readers can use the survey to distinguish an observed result in one setup from a broader statement about a model's abilities.
论文将提示视为研究和激发语言模型推理的一种方式，而不是可以随意互换的单一技巧。它的贡献是对研究工作的比较性综合，配合面向初学者的系统资源，并讨论推理能力可能出现的原因。核心阅读视角是把一条关于提示的主张，连接到支撑它的任务、模型回答和比较。这个视角很重要，因为提示可以改变问题的呈现方式，却不意味着每个任务都同样能说明推理。读者可以据此区分：某个设置中的观察结果，和关于模型能力的更宽泛陈述。

title: Method
方法
html: Its method is literature synthesis rather than a training pipeline or an experiment that trains one new system. The authors introduce research works through comparisons and summaries, then provide a resource collection and discuss future directions. For each cited study, keep four objects visible: the prompt supplied to the model, the reasoning task, the resulting response, and the evaluation used to judge that response. These objects form a compact reading record for a method: changing any one of them can change what a reported result establishes. The survey therefore supports comparison across papers, while the original studies remain necessary for exact examples, model settings, and measurements.

本文的方法是文献综合，而不是训练一个新系统的流程，也不是一项单独的新实验。作者通过比较和总结介绍研究工作，随后提供资源集合并讨论未来方向。对每项被引研究，都应持续关注四个对象：给模型的提示、推理任务、得到的回答，以及判定该回答的评测。这四个对象构成了理解方法的简明记录：其中任何一个改变，都可能改变一项结果实际说明了什么。因此，综述支持跨论文比较；但要核对具体示例、模型设置和测量方式，仍须回到原始研究。

title: Evidence
证据
html: The paper's evidence is its organized coverage of existing research rather than a newly collected benchmark score or a single controlled experiment. The official abstract promises comparisons and summaries, so a useful reading habit is to return to a cited primary paper before treating two reported results as directly comparable. Ask whether the papers use the same task formulation, prompt information, model setting, and success measure. Task construction and prompt format can change what a score means, especially when a task accepts only a final answer while another also studies an intermediate explanation. The survey is strongest as evidence for how the literature is organized and where a claim came from; it does not erase differences among the primary evaluations.

本文的证据是对既有研究的有组织覆盖，而不是新收集的基准分数或单一受控实验。官方摘要承诺给出比较和总结，因此在把两个结果视为可直接比较之前，应回到被引原始论文。要问：两篇论文是否使用相同的任务表述、提示信息、模型设置和成功指标？任务构造和提示格式会改变分数的含义，尤其是一项任务只接受最终答案，而另一项还考察中间解释时。综述最适合用来确认文献如何被组织、某项主张来自哪里；它不会消除各原始评测之间的差异。

title: Novelty
新意
html: This survey does not claim a new prompting algorithm, a universal evaluation, or a single explanation of reasoning. Its distinctive value is to make a rapidly growing literature readable through a common comparison-oriented account, while also collecting systematic resources and highlighting possible explanations and future work. Earlier primary papers usually establish the individual prompting results; this paper makes their assumptions and contrasts easier to inspect together. Its novelty is therefore organizational and interpretive. That helps separate a memorable method name from the task, comparison, and evidence behind it, and it helps a reader notice when two similarly named methods are evaluated under materially different conditions.

这篇综述并未提出新的提示算法、通用评测或单一的推理解释。它的独特价值在于以统一、面向比较的方式使快速增长的文献更易阅读，同时收集系统资源并指出可能的解释与未来工作。较早的原始论文通常确立各自的提示结果；本文使这些结果的假设和差异更容易被放在一起检查。因此，它的新意主要在组织与解释层面。这有助于区分一个容易记住的方法名称，和其背后的任务、比较及证据，并注意到名称相似的方法是否在实质不同的条件下评测。

title: Limitations
局限
html: Because it summarizes many studies, the survey cannot make their task settings identical or turn their results into one common leaderboard. A reported improvement may depend on a particular prompt, model, set of demonstrations, or task formulation, and the survey itself does not supply one shared experimental protocol. It also cannot replace the detailed methods and evaluation sections of every work it cites. Use it to identify relevant work and comparison questions, then inspect primary sources for exact inputs, output requirements, model versions, and measurements. Do not infer that a prompting result will transfer to a different problem simply because the paper labels both problems as reasoning.
由于总结了大量研究，综述无法让它们的任务设置完全一致，也不能把这些结果变成同一张统一排行榜。报告的提升可能依赖某个提示、模型、示例集合或任务表述，综述本身也没有提供共享的实验协议。它同样不能替代每篇被引工作的详细方法和评测部分。可用它定位相关工作和比较问题，再查原始来源的具体输入、输出要求、模型版本和测量方式。不要仅因两个问题都被称为推理，就推断某个提示结果会迁移到另一个问题。

title: Usefulness
用途
html: Read this paper when you need a defensible starting point for prompting-based reasoning research or when a paper list contains unfamiliar method names. It is especially useful for turning a vague question—such as whether a prompt improves reasoning—into concrete checks about task type, information supplied by the prompt, comparison system, and stated future direction. The linked resource collection is a practical entry point for further reading. For a project, it can help formulate a small comparison table before choosing a primary paper: what is being asked, what the prompt adds, what response is evaluated, and what conclusion the result can reasonably support.
当你需要为基于提示的推理研究选择可靠起点，或面对一份包含陌生方法名称的论文列表时，可读本文。它特别适合把“提示是否改善推理”这类模糊问题，转成对任务类型、提示提供的信息、比较系统和所述未来方向的具体检查。链接的资源集合也是继续阅读的实用入口。做项目时，可以先用它建立一个小型比较表，再选择原始论文：问了什么、提示增加了什么、评测哪种回答，以及结果能够合理支持什么结论。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html: Start with the paper's account of the research landscape and its comparisons, then use the resource list to follow a method or task that matters to you. While reading, write down what the prompt supplies, whether it changes the requested response, and what the evaluation asks the model to do. Mark which statements summarize a cited paper and which statements compare several papers. Then read at least one primary study behind a result you plan to reuse. This keeps a prompt-level observation from being mistaken for a general capability claim and makes it easier to recognize when an apparent improvement follows from a changed task presentation rather than a like-for-like comparison.
先看论文对研究版图和比较的叙述，再利用资源列表追踪你关心的方法或任务。阅读时记下提示提供了什么、它是否改变了所要求的回答，以及评测要求模型做什么。标记哪些陈述是在概述一篇被引论文，哪些是在比较多篇论文。随后，至少阅读一篇支撑你计划复用结果的原始研究。这样可避免把提示层面的观察误当成普遍能力主张，也更容易发现表面上的提升是否来自任务呈现发生变化，而非可直接对照的比较。
